name: Tolstoyan movement
summary: Tolstoyans follow Leo Tolstoy's reading of Jesus's Sermon on the Mount as a rule of life: love enemies, never resist evil by force, take no oaths. From this they conclude that the state, army, police, courts and the established church rest on organised violence and should be withdrawn from, not reformed or overthrown by force. Many also reject private landownership, money power and luxury and live simply on the land, often as vegetarians and chaste, in voluntary colonies.
scope: The Christian-anarchist, nonresistant teaching of the later Leo Tolstoy (c. 1880-1910), mainly The Kingdom of God Is Within You (1893), Patriotism and Government (1900) and The Slavery of Our Times (1900), together with the Tolstoyan colonies and followers (Chertkov, Gandhi's correspondence) as described in the movement article. Tolstoy discouraged treating his views as a fixed doctrine, so answers follow his writings, not any organisation. Excludes his earlier novels' conservative aristocratic outlook.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Tolstoy opposed state-run schemes funded by taxes extracted under threat; care is a duty of neighbours acting voluntarily, so a state healthcare programme is inferred to be unwelcome.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: A legal wage floor is a coercive law in his definition of legislation as organised violence, though he sympathised with workers' plight; inferred, not discussed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He did not defend markets: he attacked money, wage labour and rent-taking, while also rejecting state direction, so the claim is not endorsed.

public-ownership.rationale: Handing industry to the state would enlarge an apparatus resting on violence, which he wanted dissolved rather than empowered.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He held taxes are imposed by the powerful and mostly serve the governing classes, so he would not ask the state to tax anyone; the wealthy should rather give up wealth voluntarily.

unions-good.rationale: He sympathised with exploited workers but wanted people to leave wage labour and factories, not organise within them; adherents are not clearly for or against unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: He denied that private ownership of land is a right, arguing it arose from conquest and is upheld by the army, and tried to renounce his own property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation is more state coercion; his remedy is abolishing organised violence, not directing corporations by law. Inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: He rejected state welfare as tax-funded coercion yet demanded radical personal charity and sharing; the statement's dependency framing is not his.

worker-ownership.rationale: He wanted the land worked by those who live on it, which resembles worker ownership, but he rejected collective economic schemes that need coercion.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Terror is no excuse for state violence in his view, and he held that governments are the chief producers of organised violence; surveillance as state coercion is rejected.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Followers shunned tobacco and alcohol personally but opposed using state force to prevent others; the legal question is not a Tolstoyan concern, so split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: He opposed censorship (his own works were censored) and any enforcement by state violence, though he condemned hatred; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: He argued every means of choosing rulers fails and that holding power corrupts, so concentrated rule is repugnant to him.

state-harmful.rationale: He called the state organised violence with no justification in modern times and urged people to stop obeying it.

limit-guns.rationale: He wanted no one to use violence at all, which would mean no guns, but he would not have the state disarm people by force.

empower-police-military.rationale: He rejected the army and police as instruments of violence and called on conscripts to refuse service.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Tolstoyans promoted chastity and condemned prostitution as exploitation (as in Resurrection), though the state should not punish by force; leaning disagree on moral grounds.

decide-locally.rationale: He wanted voluntary, small communities in place of the nation-state, which accords with local decision, but he opposed any government.

rehabilitation.rationale: He argued punishment brutalises and does not reduce crime, which favours rehabilitation over punishment, though he opposed prisons altogether.

traditional-family.rationale: He valued chastity and opposed the institution of marriage in his late writing, so the statement about traditional family as foundation is not his view.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Tolstoy rejected marriage as an institution and his late sexual ethics were ascetic; adherents have no common view on legalising it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Taking life is forbidden by his reading of the commandment against killing, so adherents would disapprove of abortion; inferred, as it is little documented.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He urged love of all people and rejected state-led programmes; adherents would back personal repentance but not state action.

gender-social-construct.rationale: He did not frame the matter this way; no documented Tolstoyan stance, so split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He called patriotism harmful and said defending national customs only divides people.

gradual-change.rationale: He believed change comes through individual moral conversion, not institutions, and rejected revolution; but not gradual reform of institutions either.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He saw peoples as a brotherhood and the fatherland as an illusion maintained by governments, so border restriction runs against it.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He opposed all governments, so giving more power to a supranational one would not be endorsed.

free-trade.rationale: He said trade and communication made peoples interdependent, but he did not defend free trade as a policy and attacked capitalism.

nation-first.rationale: Patriotism is called an unnatural, irrational and harmful feeling, and preferring one's own nation comes at others' expense.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Military force is forbidden to a Christian under his reading of nonresistance, whatever the aim.

open-borders.rationale: He wanted people to see themselves as a brotherhood and not as subjects of a fatherland, which fits eventually open borders, though he never made it a programme.

limit-growth.rationale: His ideal was a simple, ascetic life close to the land, which accords with limiting growth, but the environmental rationale is anachronistic.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; he favoured simple living but opposed government coercion, pulling in opposite directions.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: He saw modern industry as removing people from nature and freedom and counted mass culture and state progress as little help.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his distrust of industrial, state-run technology and his opposition to militarism.

revolution-justified.rationale: He doubted violent overthrow lessens violence, since a new power would be as oppressive, and agreed with anarchists only about the existing order.

experts-over-public.rationale: He distrusted every group that holds power over others, including educated elites, and held authority corrupts; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: He argued communal schemes would need coercion to allot work and would reintroduce compulsory labour.

socialized-markets.rationale: He wanted neither wage labour nor state ownership; not a question he addressed.

land-value-tax.rationale: He became a strong advocate of Georgism and explored it in Resurrection, though a tax is state coercion in his own principle.

tax-inheritance.rationale: He denied property rights in land and renounced his own inheritance, but opposed taxes as plunder by the state; split.

basic-income.rationale: A state payment funded by taxes imposed by force would be resisted; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tariffs serve nationalism and state power, which he opposed; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state directing the economy would extend its organised violence, contrary to his remedy of abolishing it.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He wanted land with those who work it but denied that land can be property at all.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He criticised wage labour as slavery of our time and money as a tool of that slavery, but gave no scheme for abolition by decree.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; he opposed the state's money power but never discussed central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages and prices rely on state coercion, which he rejected.

one-party-rule.rationale: He rejected rule by any group using violence, and Tolstoyan communities were suppressed by the Soviet state.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He listed divine right and heredity among methods of choosing rulers that have failed, and criticised the tsarist order.

democracy-best.rationale: He held that elections and parliaments have not kept power from abuse, so democracy is not an answer, though he did not prefer other states.

direct-votes.rationale: Voting is participation in the state he refused to join; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Another structure of political power rests on coercion, so he would not endorse it.

right-to-secede.rationale: He would not support force to keep a nation together, but also opposed forming new nations; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: He argued power makes holders put the public interest below their own and that no method yields trustworthy rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nonresistance to evil by force is the core of his teaching, including defensive violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: He saw war as the product of governments and patriotism and condemned it absolutely.

separate-church-state.rationale: He attacked the Orthodox Church for being subservient to the state, but he wanted both to wither, not a negotiated separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He held Christ's teaching cannot be imposed by force and is accepted by inner conviction, so legislating it is wrong.

private-courts-defense.rationale: He rejected courts and armed force in any hands, as they rest on violence.

military-superiority.rationale: He held armies and arms races to be fruits of patriotism and rulers' interests, and urged abandonment of both.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He taught the brotherhood of peoples and called nation-based loyalty harmful.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He saw history as shaped by organised violence by rulers, and rejected resisting by force; not class struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He wanted sharing and voluntary equality of living but not state engineering of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: He denied that anyone owns land through conquest but did not address indigenous claims.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Repentance and giving are Christian duties, but state-demanded reparation is coercive; split.

civilizational-union.rationale: He condemned national and religious divisions and rejected any new state union.

self-interest-moral.rationale: His ethics centred on love of neighbour and renunciation of wealth and self.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He stressed duties to God and neighbour over claims against others, but rejected duties imposed by state or community force.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Vegetarianism and simple life on the land suggest respect for nature, though his case was moral and not environmental.

limit-population.rationale: He promoted chastity but opposed state measures; inferred and low.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He lamented the pull of factories from the village and rejected much of modern Western culture.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He valued rural simplicity over disruptive industry; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not discussed; his ascetic ethos suggests scepticism.

algorithmic-government.rationale: It would extend state coercion, which he wanted ended.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; sympathy for private persons against states is balanced by no concern with the topic.

restore-past-order.rationale: He criticised the existing order and the church, and sought a new Christian life, not a restored one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He held to a moral principle regardless of consequences, rejecting expedient calculation.

direct-action.rationale: He urged refusal to serve, pay or obey rather than elections, though in a nonviolent, individual form.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nonviolence applies to the means as well as the ends, so violence cannot bring a peaceful society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: His colonies were agrarian, with farm labour as the ideal, not hunter-gathering.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: He urged everyone to do manual labour on the land and criticised monotonous, commanded factory labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: His ethic was giving to others as they need, but not as a state arrangement.

production-for-use.rationale: He preferred subsistence on the land to production for markets; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He wrote that workers are enslaved by those who own land and capital and hold power by violence.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He rejected any dictatorial power held by force and sceptical of revolutionary seizures of power.

collective-farming.rationale: Colonies farmed communally in Tolstoyan practice, but they were voluntary and not mandated; split.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He blamed governments and patriotism for war more than capitalism as such.

taxation-theft.rationale: He said taxes were never established by consent and are plunder, and Tolstoyans refused them, though he did not use the libertarian language.

harm-principle.rationale: He denied the state any right to restrict by force, which goes beyond this, and would add that moral standards are higher.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Not a question he framed in rights terms.

conscription.rationale: He argued conscripts become responsible for state violence and urged refusal.

exit-over-voice.rationale: He never compared leaving a country with voting; he rejected both the state and participation in elections, so no stance can be inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Governments are not legitimate to him, so running them as firms is no remedy.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; he did hold that landlessness enslaves workers.

media-academia-power.rationale: He claimed that schools, press and church hypnotise the people for rulers, but denied that elected officials hold real power over the state.

hereditarian-race.rationale: He rejected national and racial divisions among people as children of God.

organic-representation.rationale: Any scheme of representation is a method of choosing rulers and fails.

total-state.rationale: The reverse of his anarchist rejection of the state.

national-rebirth.rationale: He treated nationalist enthusiasms as harmful, and wanted moral renewal of individuals instead.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He saw conquest as violence and patriotism as its source.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: He rejected oaths and rule by violence.

bound-labor.rationale: He condemned slavery in all forms, including compelled labour for landowners.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: He held that schools teach obedience and superstition for rulers, but he also held to universal moral truths.

universal-morality.rationale: His ethics derive from Christ's commandments as universal, but he took them from conscience and the heart, not reason alone.

single-common-good.rationale: He held love as a universal good but rejected political organisation of it.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He rejected nation-states and their claims to land.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to nationality-based citizenship offsets support for free movement.

revive-national-language.rationale: State promotion of national identity is contrary to his view of patriotism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not a Tolstoyan concern; he sought to leave factory work.

school-vouchers.rationale: He wanted free voluntary education away from state schools, but not tax-funded vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Public borrowing and fiscal policy are outside his writings, and he opposed taxation and state economic management generally, so no stance is inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: He wanted freedom from state violence but did not value markets or capital; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: His programme is moral example without laws or punishments, as in return of good for evil.

national-self-determination.rationale: He rejected nations as basis for politics but also opposed forced domination.

force-without-un.rationale: Force abroad is rejected whatever approvals exist.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He grounded his ethics in the Sermon on the Mount as faith in Christ's teaching, though without miracles or dogma.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: He held people to be a brotherhood regardless of fatherland.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He insisted all must labour but rejected coercion by the state.

class-collaboration.rationale: He urged love and no violent struggle, though he called employers' ownership unjust.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: He judged much art harshly as counterfeit, but did not call for destroying institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: A bloc of states against another is more patriotism and state power.

workers-nation.rationale: National organisation is a patriotism he rejected.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He denied that law may enforce any roles, though his own writing was traditional about women; low.

ban-interest.rationale: He condemned money power but did not propose laws against interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He condemned all violence and held all people brothers.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He described government as a pyramid of power seized by the most ruthless and used to enrich ruling classes.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his distrust of industry and state development.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: He rejected nationalist cultural demands and defended peoples' mutual openness.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiratorial nationalist idea alien to his teaching.

proportional-representation.rationale: He held no electoral system can fix government; indifferent.

national-mission.rationale: Contradicts his rejection of patriotism and force.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: He criticised the aristocracy's burden on the poor, but said little of structures favouring men.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He said power makes holders put their own interest above the public's and that governments obstruct progress.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Coercion over bodies and life contradicts his ethics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He condemned killings by state forces but would stress personal repentance over legal accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He rejected even a minimal state, since defence, courts and police all rest on violence.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Everyone is a child of God and part of a brotherhood of peoples.

socialism-one-country.rationale: He was not a socialist and did not address the question.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: He held that landholding by conquest is unjust but did not discuss settler states.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: He sought no state codes at all.

restrict-conversion.rationale: He held faith must come by inner conviction, and was himself excommunicated for dissent.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: He urged vegetarianism by example but not law, and opposed state compulsion.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: He criticised state schools for teaching religious superstition and church doctrine, though he rejected state schools more generally.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The state should wither, not grow.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He denied that taxes or laws rest on consent and held authority rests on violence; he would not call any state legitimate.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist national goals follow patriotism; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Coercion against a minority contradicts nonresistance.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He rejected force in all circumstances, including defensive.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: He saw struggle between nations as harmful, and love as the principle.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: He opposed some holding arbitrary power over others, but his remedy is no state at all.

separated-powers.rationale: He held that arranging bodies of government does not remove its violence.

vanguard-party.rationale: He rejected the seizure of power by disciplined parties.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He wanted the privileged to give up wealth and held the aristocracy burdens the poor, but not via law.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing did not exist in his time; his only property doctrine concerns land, which he held cannot be owned, so the question lies outside his teaching.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: He noted that strikes by workers are repressed while capitalists' are encouraged, hence he would object to restrictions, though he opposed state laws generally.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He blamed landholding and state violence for poverty, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He held that peoples are brothers and that divisions are from governments.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Any office-holding is power over others; lottery is no remedy.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He rejected state violence in all circumstances.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State fixing of prices is law by coercion; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: He was censored and opposed state control of thought.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: He rejected the nationalist basis of citizenship.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: He would want no one enriched by office, but rejected representation itself.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding oaths and discipline conflict with his insistence on individual conscience.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He opposed all governments, though he favoured brotherhood of peoples.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He rejected both armed forces and rulers' power.

church-by-bishops.rationale: He rejected the hierarchy of the Orthodox Church and was excommunicated.

clerical-rule.rationale: He criticised the church for subservience to state and held authority corrupt.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: He urged refusal of service rather than aiding any side's victory, though not defeat sought by violence; leaning agree on opposing own government's war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: He judged art by its moral effect and rejected elite art, but he was censored himself and rejected state enforcement.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: He opposed holding of rulers' power; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Not his programme; he saw elections as no cure.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He opposed armies and military alliances as products of governments.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: He rejected property rights in land but not tenants' arrangements by law.

people-in-arms.rationale: Violence is wrong whoever holds the arms.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: He held that estrangement from nature in factories is the root misery, and the colonies were agrarian.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Nationalist aims are rejected, though no state violence.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: He said elite culture and art alienated the people and held manual labour as moral; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He held that preferring one's people is harmful and all are brothers.

death-penalty.rationale: He condemned gibbets and guillotines and argued Christ forbids killing.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: His emphasis on chastity and criticism of state schooling suggests opposition.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: He opposed state-taught religious doctrine in schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: He preached chastity but against law enforcement; split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Nationality as a basis for state membership is rejected.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; he rejected state nationalism but also state control.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Tolstoyans sought exemption from conscription and oaths for conscience's sake.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: He broke with convention himself and saw conformity as obedience to superiors; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: He did not discuss international lending; he opposed state taxation and nationalism, but also nothing in his teaching speaks to debts between governments.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He rejected independence as a goal but wanted land reform.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Violence over others for development contradicts his teaching.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He urged the privileged to give, but not by state transfer.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: He held that no method of choosing rulers, election included, keeps power trustworthy.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is outside his writing; he distrusted the state and money power alike, so he gives no reason to prefer either.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: He held that attachment to national territory is part of the harmful patriotism sustaining wars.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: He said property taken by unjust means defeats its purpose, but went further in denying landed property altogether.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: He died in 1910 and did not address it; adherents were persecuted under Soviet rule and would not call it socialist, but no common view.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is anachronistic and he wished no state coercion, though his simple living favoured caution; adherents give no common answer.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliances for defence are military force and patriotism extended.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He opposed the church's union with state but did not want the state to hold power over clergy either.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: He rejected rulers and symbolic national unity both.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Force is excluded in every case.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy arrangements within states were not his concern, as he wanted no state at all and no regional economic system by law.

sacred-ruler.rationale: He criticised the church for sanctifying rulers and denied any ruler legitimacy.

flat-income-tax.rationale: He opposed taxation as plunder, not preferring one structure; leans disagree as it eases taxation's legitimacy.

character-from-environment.rationale: He stressed moral conversion and also environmental corruption; no clear stance.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He held that rulers' laws are organised violence and that rulers are corrupted by power.

space-expansion.rationale: Expansion as a civilisational goal is contrary to his simplicity and anti-national stance; inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: He held that arrangements of government do not cure its violence.

leader-cult.rationale: He denounced the hypnotising of people into reverence for rulers and patriotism.

equal-parenting.rationale: Court rules on custody were not addressed by him, and he distrusted courts altogether, so adherents have no shared view.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not addressed; he rejected socialism and party leaders alike.

land-redistribution.rationale: He held landholders' title came from conquest and that workers should have the land, though he sought change through renunciation and not state seizure.

refugee-return.rationale: He opposed national borders, though his focus was not on refugee rights.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Ethnic claims are the harmful patriotism he rejected.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: He was excommunicated himself and held faith to be inward conviction.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not discussed; he criticised money power but proposed no monetary arrangement between countries.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: He opposed unions based on peoples' kinship as an extension of patriotism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; he rejected national identity as political basis.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: He did not address the strategy of persecuted minorities; he opposed nationalism but also offered no view on emigration versus struggle.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He held that ideas, specifically Christian understanding of life, drive change.

ban-cartels.rationale: Another use of state coercion; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: He opposed state use of taxes for the privileged; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He rejected both courts and majority rule as sources of legitimacy.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Rejects state bodies being formed by compulsion; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: National economic blocs follow state patriotism, though he valued village self-sufficiency.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding state treaties rest on coercion; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: He wished work to be done from love and duty, not pay; Tolstoyans pursued self-sufficient labour.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: He rejected violent revolution and doubted new powers would be less oppressive.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He tried to renounce his aristocratic wealth and held that aristocracy burdens the poor.

history-own-civilization.rationale: He attacked state schools for teaching patriotic superstition.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Ruling others by force is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: He criticised schools for teaching obedience and patriotic superstition.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Admissions and hiring policies are outside his time and writing, and he did not discuss affirmative action by state.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; he opposed both state and capital power over money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: He wrote on capitalist enslavement but made no prediction about crises or collapse, as his remedy was moral conversion and not economic breakdown.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Contradicts his rejection of patriotism and empire.

delink-world-market.rationale: His village-subsistence ideal sounds like delinking, but he never discussed poor countries' trade policy, so no stance is stated.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: He described workers as enslaved by land and capital and made no claim on a divide between workers in rich and poor countries.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: He taught universal brotherhood but opposed legal compulsion; leans disagree as a moral position.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He did not look to constitutions to restrain governments, which should dissolve.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: He said nothing on colonial treaties; his general rejection of conquest and states gives no basis for deciding their validity.

elective-rulers.rationale: Elections are one of the methods of choosing rulers he said fail.

minority-veto.rationale: He held that no authoritative decision binds individual conscience, making individual consent central.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He ruled out resisting evil by force, though refusal to obey is encouraged.

parliament-supreme.rationale: He held parliaments no better than other methods of ruling.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: He became a vegetarian and promoted The First Step on compassion to animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: His vegetarianism rejected killing animals for food, though adherents ranged from meat-eaters to fruitarians.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: He urged the rich to give up wealth, but rejected the privilege assumed in the premise.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Tolstoyans withdraw from government and refuse to take part in state affairs.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: He said that schools, press and church hypnotise people into obedience, so this rings broadly true.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: He said rulers keep power by stoking patriotism and teaching obedience through schools, press and church, as well as force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: He explained poverty by landholding and state violence within societies and wrote no theory of a world economy.

native-born-offices.rationale: It rests on nationality, which he rejected.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist party relations do not concern him; he rejected party politics altogether, so the question does not arise.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He wanted self-sufficient village life, but also giving.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial claims fuel the wars he condemned.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: He opposed political leadership by any group.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; he would oppose fascism but not make constitutions.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He died before fascism and Soviet rule and did not rank regimes; he condemned all state violence, but adherents were persecuted by one in particular.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: He condemned slavery in all forms, but did not discuss the American Civil War.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Policy attention by sex is not addressed in his work, and he looked to personal repentance not state programmes.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: He condemned all violence equally, but did not address policy.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He opposed all government as such.

military-guardian-role.rationale: He rejected the army and any political role for it.

paid-care-work.rationale: He valued work done for love and condemned wage labour, so paying for care is neither endorsed nor condemned in his writings.

filial-duty.rationale: He wished love and respect but he himself broke with family expectations.

office-by-exam.rationale: He held office-holding corrupts; remedy is not different selection.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism is patriotism by another name.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: He opposed marriage as institution, so he would accept ending it without state-imposed conditions; low.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is outside his writings; he opposed both state taxation and capital's power, giving no basis to choose.

land-use-tenure.rationale: He argued land should not be property, and Georgism holds that land belongs to all, worked by those who use it.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed; he held parliaments no check.

single-official-language.rationale: He rejected using the state to impose national identity.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: It rests on nationality, contrary to brotherhood; he also denied private land ownership altogether.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Legal tests of discrimination are outside his thinking, and he sought moral change rather than courts.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Tolstoyans pursue an ascetic, simple life and Tolstoy renounced wealth.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Violence is excluded, as is fuelling it.

corporate-influence.rationale: He said the powerful capture the state, but his remedy is not regulation.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: It serves nationalist state interest; he rejected state controls.

residents-only-property.rationale: He rejected property in land and nationalist exclusion.

job-guarantee.rationale: State employment extends the state; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: He held that liberal as well as despotic states rest on violence.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: He taught refusing taxes, oaths and conscription and saw laws as organised violence.

non-intervention.rationale: He opposed all state violence abroad, though he rejected sovereignty claims too.

industrial-unions.rationale: He did not discuss union structure, and wanted workers to leave factory work for the land.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: It fuels hatred between peoples, which he condemned.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: He opposed marriage as an institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: He was himself censored and favoured free circulation of ideas.

local-production.rationale: He favoured village subsistence close to the land.

informal-organisation.rationale: Tolstoy discouraged any fixed doctrine or organisation, and followers formed voluntary communities.

national-law-over-international.rationale: He rejected national sovereignty claims but did not support international law either.

religious-nation.rationale: He opposed national identity and church-state fusion.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal sharing between regions is a state matter he did not address, since he wished taxes abolished with the state.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: He wanted common land but not communal personal belongings; inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: He rejected violent confrontation of any ideology.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Delivery of public services is not covered; he objected to the state's coercive base rather than its management.

religion-illusion.rationale: His ethics came from Jesus's teaching, which he took as true.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He saw industrial capitalism as enslaving and removing people from nature.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: He wrote on marriage and chastity but not on the economic basis of women's equality, so no stance is stated.

socialized-care.rationale: He held family and local community duties are personal and not state services; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties between governments and peoples within them are not discussed, and he regarded governments' agreements as backed by violence.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Tolstoyan colonies were voluntary self-governing agrarian communities sharing property.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-driven ethnic settlement is coercion and nationalism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He rejected both capitalist ownership and socialist schemes needing coercion in favour of a Christian third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: It is a nationalist claim and fuels wars.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Contradicts his commitment to truth and brotherhood; inferred, since the event is later than he lived.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: He opposed state punishment of any kind.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He rejected state violence and was censored himself.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He was excommunicated and held faith can't be coerced.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Forcible rule for economic gain is plunder he condemned.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Armed resistance is excluded even in defence.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: He rejected violence even against unjust rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He favoured voluntary community decisions, but refused democratic participation in the state.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: He described oppression as flowing from state violence and landholding, but did not theorise overlap among race, sex and class.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The question is anachronistic and his late sexual ethics were ascetic, so no shared adherent position can be inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: He held life sacred and opposed killing; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: He rejected parties and the whole political system; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: He described factory work as losing contact with nature and freedom, forced into monotonous commanded labour.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Such cultural exclusion is the patriotism he rejected.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He held that God's law of love is supreme but no ruler has divine authority; split on wording.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: He did not address dress in state institutions; he opposed the state church and also state coercion on conscience, so no stance is clear.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment contract law is outside his thinking, and he said little on harassment as a workplace matter.

social-market-economy.rationale: He rejected both state direction and markets; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Conscripts should refuse service and armies should disappear.

rich-first.rationale: He held concentrated wealth unjust and urged giving it up.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He opposed all blocs and wars, though the position is more radical than neutrality.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Heredity is one of the rejected methods of choosing rulers.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: He criticised money power but proposed no credit institutions; voluntary mutual aid fits his ethic, but no text endorses banks of this kind.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: International lending conditions are anachronistic, and he addressed taxes and state finance only to condemn them.

property-franchise.rationale: He criticised privilege based on property and any voting that props up the state.

reification.rationale: He criticised relations of domination through money and law, but did not develop the theory that social relations appear as relations between things.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: He wrote that wealth produced by workers is taken by a few and that press and schools serve rulers.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: He held laws are organised violence, but also arbitrary decrees worse; not his question.

online-participation.rationale: The internet postdates him, and he refused to take part in state decisions in any form, so no stance is stated.

open-government-data.rationale: He was himself censored and valued free circulation of ideas, but he never discussed access to state records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: He held that conscience is not to be restricted by law.

citizens-assembly.rationale: It is another way of choosing who rules; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: He reinterpreted Christianity around the Sermon on the Mount, discarding dogma and miracles.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He said wealth in a few hands rests on violence and enslaves workers.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: He opposed any military service for anyone.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He rejected state promotion of belief of any kind.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He argued prisons and gibbets brutalise and that police rest on violence.

more-religion-public.rationale: He wanted Christianity as private conviction freed from the state-allied church and denied religious bodies any public power.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed; he rejected state claims to territory, but also coercive annexation.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Sending troops into another state is military force, excluded by nonresistance.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: He called for personal giving and sharing and rejected tax-funded state schemes as coercive, though he also held charity does not cure the exploitation behind poverty.

term-limits.rationale: He rejected every method of choosing rulers, so limiting their terms was beside the point; not discussed.

vote-delegation.rationale: He urged withdrawing from state politics and held voting gives power its sanction, so delegable voting is inferred to be unwelcome.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; he opposed war and the arms burden, but a state-led policy priority is not his frame.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: He rejected the church hierarchy and priestly offices altogether, so a bar on women has no place in his view; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: He condemned lust and the domination of women in marriage in his late writing; inferred, though his own household was not equal.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Tolstoy rejected taking part in elections as complicity in state violence, so a local vote for foreigners is inferred to be of no interest to him.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from his opposition to state coercion; he wanted land rent returned to the community by moral change, not capped by law.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of ownership as a means of exploiting others; he gave up the copyright on his later works.

uniformed-youth.rationale: He condemned patriotism and the military training of the young as schooling in organised violence.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Weapons of mass killing were never discussed; inferred from his absolute rejection of violence and of the army.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign bases were not discussed; inferred from his rejection of armies, war and national military alliances.

recognise-genocide.rationale: He did not address formal state recognition; he would both condemn mass killing and distrust state declarations.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: He held that living off land and capital ownership enslaves workers, and that people should live by their own labour.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Non-resistance to evil by force is the core Tolstoyan teaching, extended to self-defence and defence of others.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: He called patriotism a deception and nations artificial divisions maintained by governments.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Never discussed; inferred from his essentialist view of sex and his ascetic, chaste ideal.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Never discussed and not a Tolstoyan concern; no position can be inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: He attacked the glorification of those who die for country as patriotic deception that serves governments.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: He saw life as a moral and religious struggle, though he rejected politics as a field for it; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Nationhood and diaspora were not his concern; he opposed national states on principle.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from his view that inner moral change must precede any social change and that the state should be withdrawn from.

god-not-male.rationale: He rejected the church's Trinity and God as person, treating God as love and spirit; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: He judged scripture by reason and the Sermon on the Mount, not by women's humanity; no direct view.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: He rejected nationalism and the privileging of any nation over others as contrary to universal love.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of national states and borders as instruments of violence.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of state coercion over workers: organisations of labourers should be free of government, though he did not endorse unions as such.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Tolstoy treated socialism as another bid to seize state power by force and rejected any class holding political power.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred: he wanted common land and voluntary service but rejected state institutions, so neither public nor private control is clearly endorsed.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of parliaments and government as organised violence; adding a chamber would not be wanted.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from his view that land belongs to all and should not be private, but he rejected the state and gave no programme of municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from his vision of voluntary, stateless communities cooperating without rulers.

family-wage.rationale: He condemned wage slavery and demanded just treatment of labourers but did not address a family wage.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred from his simple, natural living and distrust of modern doctors and industrial civilisation; faster approval is not something he would press for.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from his acceptance of death as natural and his rejection of luxury and state-funded schemes.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: he opposed taxation and money power as tools of violence but never addressed payment tracing.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; his hostility to state coercion suggests sympathy but he said nothing on online identity.

person-over-state.rationale: Conscience before state commands is central: he refused to treat people as instruments of government, army or taxation.

spiritual-nature.rationale: His teaching is a religious ethic of inner moral life, with material striving subordinated to spiritual growth.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of state power generally; revocable powers rest on a national legislature he would not accept.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from his preference for simple agrarian life and suspicion of industrial technology.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from his condemnation of city life and luxury and his call to live by working the land.

racial-group-interests.rationale: He rejected nationalism and group loyalties as sources of division and violence, urging universal brotherhood.

racial-pride.rationale: He condemned patriotism and pride in one's nation as sinful and as a basis for war.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He rejected armies and all war, even defensive; nonresistance forbids violence in any cause.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Patriotism and Government treats nations and patriotism as tools of governments to divide humanity, and Tolstoy held that all people are brothers in Christ.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: Tolstoy rejected taking part in state politics and voting, and the sources show no support for electorates divided by religion.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Patriotism and Government argues governments stir fear of foreign enemies to justify armies, and Tolstoyans reject patriotic panic as organised deception.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: Tolstoy opposed state schemes paid for by taxes taken under threat, though he valued teaching the poor.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: he rejected state taxation and coercion in general, so a state pollution tax would not be welcomed.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from his call to live simply on the land and not exploit nature or others; the sources do not address it directly.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources do not say that women bring distinct values; Tolstoy's views on women were contested and unsettled among followers.

arms-reduction.rationale: Tolstoyans demand the abolition of armies and refuse military service, so cuts to armaments agree with them though they deny any need for national defence.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: he held that governments deceive peoples through war and patriotism, which implies concealed dealings are illegitimate.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: he blamed state and capital together for oppression and rejected coercive state power, so state capital controls are not endorsed.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Tolstoy held that the army and police are organised violence that Christians must not support, so strengthening a state arms monopoly runs against his teaching of nonresistance.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Kingdom of God Is Within You calls on Christians to refuse military service and Patriotism and Government condemns wars between states.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Tolstoy sympathised with workers but did not endorse union bargaining or strikes as such; sources do not address it.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: He saw taxes as plunder backed by threat and wage labour as slavery, so a tax-funded wage top-up is inferred to be rejected.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Tolstoy rejected legislation and taxation as violence rather than seeking to regulate state borrowing; no direct discussion.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He condemned economic exploitation but rejected remedies by state or treaty rules; inferred, not discussed.

smash-state-machine.rationale: He wanted the state to dissolve by people's withdrawal and condemned violent revolution, though he equally rejected using the state; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: He urged voluntary simple living and land sharing but refused to fix a doctrine or system; adherents differ.

nature-as-capital.rationale: He opposed private landownership and money power, so pricing nature as an asset is inferred to be unwelcome.

sacred-nation.rationale: Patriotism and Government rejects patriotism and the nation as a basis of loyalty, calling it contrary to Christianity.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; he opposed tax-funded schemes yet condemned debt bondage.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; he condemned exploitation by landowners and the state generally, not by regions.

shared-human-nature.rationale: He taught the equal worth of all people as children of God, but the sources do not discuss human nature as a fixed basis; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: State funding rests on taxation he called coercive, and he distrusted state-controlled schooling and press; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Tolstoy later held that the moral teachings of all great religions, such as Buddhism, Confucianism and Christianity, share one core of love and nonresistance, though he put Christ's teaching first; inferred from the movement article.

farm-price-support.rationale: Tolstoy opposed state schemes funded by coerced taxes and held that landowning and money power enslave the farmer; he wanted abolition of land rent, not price guarantees.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Tolstoy held that refusing to resist evil by force and opposing armies and war follow from the Sermon on the Mount, so possessing weapons of mass killing is rejected.

workers-own-party.rationale: Tolstoy rejected parliaments and parties as organs of the state's violence and urged withdrawal from politics; inferred, as he did not address labour parties directly.

ban-fgm.rationale: Tolstoy's love-of-neighbour ethic is inferred to oppose mutilation of children, but he opposed enforcing even good ends by state coercion, so the support is weak.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Tolstoy opposed private landownership for all and held land to be common, but also rejected legislation by the state; adherents have no settled view on legal inheritance.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The sources never address language; inferred from Tolstoy's universalism and rejection of nationalist divisions that the language is one.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Tolstoy rejected courts and legal coercion, so legal liability enforced by the state is inferred to be unwelcome, though he condemned harm to neighbours.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Tolstoy rejected all state and traditional authority backed by violence, including hereditary rulers, so an official role in lawmaking is rejected.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Tolstoy's simple-living, vegetarian followers valued nature over luxury and consumption, but he rejected state compulsion, so the support is weak; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Tolstoy held that courts and punishment are organised violence, and mandatory sentences extend state coercion further.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Tolstoy rejected state compulsion and nationalist divisions, so a legal duty to learn the national language is inferred to be rejected.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Tolstoy rejected compulsion in all forms but also distrusted wage-labour institutions and organised pressure; he never addressed closed shops, so this is a split inference from his rejection of coercion.

voter-id.rationale: Tolstoy held that voting and electoral machinery merely legitimise organised violence, so he would not favour adding enforcement conditions to it; inferred from his critique of choosing rulers.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Tolstoy rejected the established church and any state-backed creed, so no interpretation of religion should have legal precedence; he himself was excommunicated for his reading of Christianity.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Tolstoy argued that elected governments still rest on organised violence, so free elections do not make a state legitimate or good; he did not accept procedure as the test.

premarital-sex.rationale: Many Tolstoyans practised chastity, and the later Tolstoy condemned sex outside or even within marriage as degrading, though he applied this to men and women alike.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Tolstoy's view that state coercion to maintain order is organised violence, and his campaigns against censorship.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Tolstoy opposed state taxation and state welfare backed by threat of force, though he sympathised with land-value taxation; inferred, so a state cash scheme is unwelcome.

women-suffrage.rationale: Tolstoy rejected voting and holding office as participation in state violence for everyone, so he would not campaign for these rights; inferred from his general critique of the state, not from a statement on women.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Tolstoy blamed church and state institutions for oppression but saw true Christianity as liberating; inferred, and he was himself conservative on women's roles.

race-social-construct.rationale: Tolstoy rejected nations and patriotism and held all people to be brothers, but the scientific claim about racial categories is outside his writings.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Tolstoy opposed new state organs and ministries as instruments of coercion; inferred from his rejection of government.

missingStatements.text: A Christian should refuse to swear oaths to any government or ruler.
missingStatements.rationale: One of the five Tolstoyan commandments is not to swear oaths, and followers refused oaths and conscription.

missingStatements.text: Judging and punishing other people by law is contrary to true religion.
missingStatements.rationale: Tolstoy rejected courts and punishment as organised violence, and held that prisons and gibbets brutalise.

missingStatements.text: A person should refuse to pay taxes that fund war.
missingStatements.rationale: He described taxes as plunder supporting the apparatus of oppression and noted refusers as testimony.

notes: Tolstoy rejected socialism and revolutionary anarchism because both rely on coercion, so positions on economic questions come from his Christian, Georgist and anti-state writings and are often inferred. Answers on topics he never discussed are low confidence.
